title: Big bluestem biomass majority gave no repeated warming increase in four Cedar Creek tests in 2017-2022
abstract: We tested whether warming raised the frequency of big bluestem holding more than half of harvested biomass. We used 216 records from nine paired Cedar Creek plots in 2017-2022. Four tests covered ambient water and drought in two periods. Warming contrasts were +25.9, +11.1, +3.7 and -7.4 percentage points. Only the early ambient-water t interval excluded zero after four-test correction. No sign-flip diagnostic passed that correction. Allowing separate share errors of five percentage points permitted zero in all four finite-record contrast bounds. Thus the records did not show a repeated warming increase in this endpoint. These bounds do not estimate sampling error. Small moving harvest strips, one site, nine plots, model-sensitive uncertainty and no independent region limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Annual majority rates and paired warming contrasts. Intervals use a t model and four-test correction; no adjusted sign-flip diagnostic passed 0.05.
